title: Electric Machines
tagline: Magnetic circuits, transformers, DC, induction and synchronous machines
summary: Electric machines convert between electrical and mechanical energy and use most of the world’s electricity. This course analyses magnetic circuits and transformers, the principles of electromechanical energy conversion, and the construction, equivalent circuits and performance of DC, induction, synchronous and special machines.
overview: A machine turns electrical energy into motion, or motion into electrical energy. This course follows the magnetic fields that make it happen: magnetic circuits, transformers, the energy conversion that produces torque, and the machines that use it - dc, induction, and synchronous.
We build each machine from its magnetic field, and then study how the field produces the force that does the work.
outcomes: Analyse magnetic circuits and compute the flux, reluctance, and inductance
Size the current of a transformer in the windings and understand the energy conversion that produces torque
Derive the equivalent circuit of a dc machine and an induction machine
Explain the rotating field, and the synchronous and special machines

chapters.title: Magnetic circuits
chapters.summary: Reluctance, magnetic materials, hysteresis and eddy-current losses, and permanent magnets.

chapters.title: Transformers
chapters.summary: Ideal and real transformers, equivalent circuits, tests, regulation, efficiency and three-phase transformers.

chapters.title: Electromechanical energy conversion
chapters.summary: Energy and co-energy, and forces and torques in singly and doubly excited systems.

chapters.title: DC machines
chapters.summary: Construction, commutation, equivalent circuit, characteristics and speed control of DC motors and generators.

chapters.title: AC machine fundamentals
chapters.summary: Distributed windings, the rotating magnetic field, and induced voltage and torque in AC machines.

chapters.title: Induction machines
chapters.summary: Equivalent circuit, torque–speed characteristic, starting and speed control of induction motors.

chapters.title: Synchronous machines
chapters.summary: Synchronous generators and motors, phasor diagrams, the power–angle characteristic and operation on an infinite bus.

chapters.title: Permanent-magnet and special machines
chapters.summary: Brushless DC and permanent-magnet synchronous motors, stepper motors and switched-reluctance motors.

history.title: Faraday's law
history.detail: Faraday showed that a changing magnetic field induces an emf, and the basis of the transformer and the machine.

history.title: Gramme ring
history.detail: One of the first dynamos, a self-exciting machine that generates a continuous supply.

history.title: Induction motor
history.description: The single-phase and polyphase induction machines.

history.title: Three-phase
history.detail: The three-phase system, the basis of the modern machine and the grid.

references.title: Electrical Machines
references.note: A clear, quantitative treatment of all the machine types, the basis of this course.

references.title: Electric Machinery and Power
references.note: The standard reference for machine analysis.

references.title: The Electric Power Industry Handbook
references.note: Power system context and the machine, at the system level.
